---
title: Deploy
guide-section: Get Started
---

Your config repo's workflow runs `scripts/deploy.sh` for you. You can also run the script by hand.

## From your config repo

The template's `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs on a self-hosted runner on your home network, since GitHub cannot reach your Home Assistant box. It checks out your config repo and the ha-automations tag, then runs `scripts/deploy.sh`.

### Setup

1. Register a self-hosted runner under **Settings > Actions > Runners**. It needs `git`, `ssh` and `rsync`, and passwordless SSH to the box.
2. Create an environment named `haos` under **Settings > Environments**.
3. Set these variables on the environment or the repo:

| variable | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `HA_SSH` | required | ssh target, e.g. `root@homeassistant.local` |
| `PACKAGE_REPO` | `<config repo owner>/ha-automations` | repo to install from; set it to `joshwlivingston/ha-automations` unless you forked |
| `HA_SSH_PORT` | `22` | ssh port |
| `RUNNER_LABELS` | `["self-hosted"]` | JSON list of runner labels |

### When it runs

- **Push to `main`:** deploys your `apps.yaml` with the latest tag.
- **New tag:** a scheduled check picks it up, every 15 minutes during the day and hourly overnight. The crons are in UTC; edit them for your time zone.
- **Manual:** **Actions > Deploy > Run workflow**, with an optional tag and a *force* box to redeploy when nothing changed.

Each run does nothing if the box already runs that tag with that `apps.yaml`.

To roll back, run it with an older tag, then disable the workflow until a fixed tag is released. Otherwise the next scheduled check reinstalls the latest tag.

## By hand

Run `scripts/deploy.sh` from a checkout of this repo (or your fork):

```sh
scripts/deploy.sh          # the version in pyproject.toml
scripts/deploy.sh v0.4.0   # a specific tag
```

### What it does

1. Checks that the tag exists on `REPO_URL`.
2. Skips the deploy if the box already runs this tag with this `apps.yaml`.
3. Copies the app shims and your `apps.yaml` to the AppDaemon add-on.
4. Sets the add-on's `python_packages` to the tagged package. Other add-on options are kept.
5. Restarts the add-on so it installs the package and loads `apps.yaml`.

### Settings

Set these in the environment or in a `.deploy.env` file at the repo root.

| setting | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `HA_SSH` | required | ssh target, e.g. `root@homeassistant.local` |
| `APPS_YAML` | required | path to your `apps.yaml`, absolute or relative to the repo root |
| `REPO_URL` | required | package source, e.g. `https://github.com/you/ha-automations` |
| `HA_SSH_PORT` | `22` | ssh port |
| `ADDON_SLUG` | `a0d7b954_appdaemon` | AppDaemon add-on slug |
| `APPS_DIR` | `/addon_configs/$ADDON_SLUG/apps` | apps directory on the box |
| `FORCE` | unset | `1` deploys even if the box already runs this tag and `apps.yaml` |
| `NO_RESTART` | unset | `1` skips the restart and prints the command instead |

Example `.deploy.env`:

```sh
HA_SSH=root@homeassistant.local
APPS_YAML=../ha-automations-config/apps.yaml
REPO_URL=https://github.com/joshwlivingston/ha-automations
```

The script header in `scripts/deploy.sh` is the source for this table.
